paper_diagnosis: Disseminated peritoneal coccidioidomycosis in pregnancy following fertility treatment
disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated peritoneal coccidioidomycosis in a newly pregnant patient
presentation_summary: 39-year-old woman underwent clomiphene citrate, HCG trigger, and intrauterine insemination, then developed intermittent fevers and abdominal pain eight days later.
She had early pregnancy with rising beta-hCG and worsening ascites, abdominal distension, fever, leukocytosis, and mild transaminitis.
At emergency presentation around 4 weeks 1 day gestation she had fever 38.2 C, WBC 17 K/uL, AST 50 U/L, ALT 80 U/L, free abdominal fluid, and later diarrhea and nausea.
By hospital day 3 she worsened to fever 39.4 C and WBC 23 K/uL; CT showed moderate ascites with omental nodularity/caking concerning for malignancy or tuberculosis.
Initial Coccidioides IgM/IgG and complement fixation titers were negative; surgical omental biopsy culture later grew Coccidioides immitis.
Only notable exposure history was travel to Palm Springs, California and construction sites in the prior two years.
